ir.name: combined_crossover_loss_fixed_signal_v2
ir.intuition: The original loss was insensitive to the objective perturbation because it only depended on the difference of log probabilities weighted by 'weight', without any interaction with the objective signal like cost_gap. To fix this, I incorporated the cost_gap as a multiplicative factor on the margin, so the loss gradient varies with changes in the objective (cost_gap). The margin x is scaled by cost_gap clamped to [-10,10] to retain numeric stability, ensuring the loss sensitivity to the objective gap. This fixes the insensitivity issue and preserves pairwise log-sigmoid formulation with weighting.
ir.pseudocode:
lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
weight = batch.get('weight', ones_like(lpw))
cost_gap = batch.get('cost_gap', batch.get('cost_b', zeros) - batch.get('cost_a', zeros))
cost_factor = clamp(cost_gap, -10, 10)
alpha = extra.get('alpha', 1.0)
x = alpha * 1.2 * cost_factor * (lpw - lpl)
x = clamp(x, -20, 20)
loss = -logsigmoid(x) * weight
return mean(loss)
ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    weight = batch.get('weight', lpw.new_ones(lpw.shape))
    zeros = lpw.new_zeros(lpw.shape)
    cost_gap = batch.get('cost_gap', batch.get('cost_b', zeros) - batch.get('cost_a', zeros))
    cost_factor = ops.clamp(cost_gap, -10.0, 10.0)
    alpha = float(extra.get('alpha', extra.get('hyperparams', {}).get('alpha', 1.0)))
    margin = ops.mul(alpha * 1.2, ops.mul(cost_factor, ops.sub(lpw, lpl)))
    margin = ops.clamp(margin, -20.0, 20.0)
    loss = ops.neg(ops.logsigmoid(margin))
    loss = ops.mul(loss, weight)
    return ops.mean(loss)
